key_facts: On information and belief, on or about August 2024, Plaintiff was hired to work at The Home Depot distribution/fulfillment center at 5395 Hopkins Road, Tracy, CA 95377. He accepted the position and began onboarding. Home Depot then ceased communication and ghosted him. No offer letter, time records, wage statements, vendor name, or adverse-action notice is in the portfolio. The complaint does not attach a Home Depot report. The load-bearing theory is information-and-belief use of § 290.46 disclosures. Supporting inference: Home Depot ordinarily backgrounds distribution-center hires; Plaintiff was on the registry; and in July 2024 First Advantage matched this same Plaintiff to SOURCE OF RECORD: CALIFORNIA SEX OFFENDER REGISTRY on the UPS report later lodged in E.D. Cal. 2:26-cv-02847. That UPS report is not alleged to have been sent to Home Depot. Labor Code § 1198.5 inspection has not yet been demanded. Serve CSC, not the Tracy building.
procedural_status: Executed verified complaint and San Joaquin intake dated September 8, 2026; signed, not yet filed. Plaintiff accepted the Tracy hire, began onboarding, and was ghosted. Hire timing remains I&B August 2024. § 290 is the third count. Lerma cannot run on an unattached Home Depot report. Serve CSC, not 5395 Hopkins Road. Do not bury Serrato disclosures that day.
damages: No wage rate or duration is in the record. Portfolio valuation is the post-favorable-MTD settlement range: $50,000 / $70,000 / $90,000. That assumes the pleading survives demurrer on notice pleading. Do not import UPS/Pilot numbers. Contingent statutory remedies if use is proven: Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) actual/treble with a $250 floor, fees, exemplary damages, or a civil penalty capped at $25,000; ICRAA § 1786.50 actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater.
risk: High-risk I&B filing: the file has no Home Depot offer, report, or notice. Lerma dismissed after the employer's report was in the record and showed ordinary court records — a demurrer cannot replicate that analysis while Home Depot withholds the report. If production later shows court records and no California-registry source, the 290 count dies then, not at the pleading stage. ICRAA is the backup path but is thinner without a named CRA. CCP § 340(a) remains a defense argument on the civil-penalty piece. Tameny is omitted. Naming the Tracy building or serving the warehouse instead of CSC would be party/service defects.
evidence: Plaintiff's statement — I&B hire on or about August 2024 at 5395 Hopkins Road, Tracy; accepted; began onboarding; then ghosted (not independently documented)
Public description of the Tracy fulfillment center at 5395 Hopkins Road (worksite identification only)

Code Civ. Proc. §§ 425.10, 452 — notice pleading; liberal construction of facts exclusively in Defendants' possession
Labor Code § 1198.5 — personnel-file inspection if Plaintiff was an employee; not yet demanded
Lerma v. Amazon, C.D. Cal. 8:22-cv-01727, Dkt. 36 — dismissal after the employer's report was in the record and showed ordinary court records, not a pleading-stage inference from an unattached report
